x86.instr.mov.description: Copies the source operand to the destination operand without modifying flags.
x86.instr.xchg.description: Swaps the contents of the two operands atomically without requiring a temporary register.
x86.instr.lea.description: Calculates the offset/address of the memory operand and stores it in the specified register. Often used for fast pointer and pointer arithmetic.
x86.instr.xlat.description: Replaces AL with the byte at DS:[BX + AL]. Useful for fast character code conversions (e.g., ASCII to 7-segment display).
x86.instr.lds.description: Loads a 32-bit far pointer from memory: 16-bit offset into destination register and 16-bit segment into DS.
x86.instr.les.description: Loads a 32-bit far pointer from memory: 16-bit offset into destination register and 16-bit segment into ES.
x86.instr.lfs.description: Loads a far pointer from memory into the destination register and segment register FS. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.lgs.description: Loads a far pointer from memory into the destination register and segment register GS. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.lss.description: Atomically loads stack pointer into destination register and SS. Disables interrupts during load to prevent invalid stack state.
x86.instr.movsx.description: Copies source operand to destination and sign-extends the value to fill the destination.
x86.instr.movzx.description: Copies source operand to destination and zero-extends the value to fill the destination.
x86.instr.movabs.summary: Move 64-bit absolute immediate (GNU as / AT&T syntax)
x86.instr.movabs.description: Mnemonic specific to the GNU Assembler (GNU as / AT&T syntax) for loading a full 64-bit immediate constant or 64-bit absolute memory address into a 64-bit register. It is not an Intel or NASM instruction mnemonic (in NASM and MASM, standard MOV RAX, imm64 is used instead).
x86.instr.bswap.description: Reverses byte order of a 32-bit or 64-bit register. Converts between Little-Endian and Big-Endian (network byte order).
x86.instr.xadd.description: Exchanges the first and second operands, then sums both and stores the result in the first operand. Used for lock-free counters.
x86.instr.cmpxchg.description: Compares accumulator (AL/AX/EAX/RAX) with destination operand. If equal, copies source to destination; otherwise copies destination to accumulator.
x86.instr.cmovz.description: Copies source to destination only if Zero Flag (ZF=1). Eliminates branch misprediction penalty.
x86.instr.cmovnz.description: Copies source to destination only if Zero Flag is clear (ZF=0).
x86.instr.cmova.description: Copies the source to the destination only when the previous unsigned comparison came out strictly greater (CF=0 and ZF=0). Reads the flags and changes none.
x86.instr.cmovae.summary: Conditional Move if Above or Equal (unsigned >=)
x86.instr.cmovae.description: Copies the source to the destination when the unsigned comparison needed no borrow (CF=0), that is, greater or equal.
x86.instr.cmovb.description: Copies the source to the destination when the unsigned comparison needed a borrow (CF=1), that is, strictly smaller.
x86.instr.cmovbe.summary: Conditional Move if Below or Equal (unsigned <=)
x86.instr.cmovbe.description: Copies the source to the destination when the unsigned comparison came out smaller or equal (CF=1 or ZF=1).
x86.instr.cmovc.description: Copies the source to the destination only if the Carry flag is set (CF=1). The same instruction as CMOVB, named after the flag instead of after the comparison.
x86.instr.cmovnc.description: Copies the source to the destination only if the Carry flag is clear (CF=0). The same instruction as CMOVAE.
x86.instr.cmovg.description: Copies the source to the destination when the signed comparison came out strictly greater (ZF=0 and SF equal to OF). Use it after comparing signed numbers; CMOVA is the unsigned counterpart.
x86.instr.cmovge.summary: Conditional Move if Greater or Equal (signed >=)
x86.instr.cmovge.description: Copies the source to the destination when the signed comparison came out greater or equal (SF equal to OF).
x86.instr.cmovl.description: Copies the source to the destination when the signed comparison came out strictly smaller (SF different from OF).
x86.instr.cmovle.summary: Conditional Move if Less or Equal (signed <=)
x86.instr.cmovle.description: Copies the source to the destination when the signed comparison came out smaller or equal (ZF=1, or SF different from OF).
x86.instr.cmovs.description: Copies the source to the destination only if the Sign flag is set (SF=1), that is, the last result had its highest bit on.
x86.instr.cmovns.summary: Conditional Move if Not Sign / Non-negative
x86.instr.cmovns.description: Copies the source to the destination only if the Sign flag is clear (SF=0).
x86.instr.cmovo.description: Copies the source to the destination only if the Overflow flag is set (OF=1): the last signed operation did not fit in its destination.
x86.instr.cmovno.description: Copies the source to the destination only if the Overflow flag is clear (OF=0).
x86.instr.cmovp.description: Copies the source to the destination only if the Parity flag is set (PF=1): the low byte of the last result held an even number of one bits.
x86.instr.cmovnp.description: Copies the source to the destination only if the Parity flag is clear (PF=0).
x86.instr.push.description: Decrements SP/ESP/RSP and copies the operand onto the top of the stack.
x86.instr.pop.description: Copies the word from the top of the stack to the destination and increments stack pointer.
x86.instr.pusha.description: Pushes AX, CX, DX, BX, original SP, BP, SI, and DI onto stack. Requires 80186+.
x86.instr.popa.description: Restores all general registers previously pushed with PUSHA. Requires 80186+.
x86.instr.pushad.description: Pushes EAX, ECX, EDX, EBX, ESP, EBP, ESI, EDI onto the stack. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.popad.description: Restores the 8 general 32-bit registers previously pushed by PUSHAD. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.pushf.description: Pushes the 16-bit FLAGS register onto the stack to save CPU status.
x86.instr.popf.description: Restores the 16-bit FLAGS register from the stack.
x86.instr.pushfd.description: Pushes the 32-bit EFLAGS register onto the stack. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.popfd.description: Restores the 32-bit EFLAGS register from the stack. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.pushfq.description: Pushes the 64-bit RFLAGS register onto the stack in 64-bit mode.
x86.instr.popfq.description: Restores the 64-bit RFLAGS register from the stack in 64-bit mode.
x86.instr.enter.description: Creates a stack frame for local variables and manages lexical nesting levels. Equivalent to PUSH BP / MOV BP, SP / SUB SP, size.
x86.instr.leave.description: Releases stack frame set up by ENTER. Equivalent to MOV SP, BP / POP BP. Requires 80186+.
x86.instr.add.description: Adds destination and source operands, storing result in destination.
x86.instr.adc.description: Adds destination, source, and Carry Flag (CF). Useful for multi-word additions.
x86.instr.sub.description: Subtracts source from destination, storing result in destination.
x86.instr.sbb.description: Subtracts source and Carry Flag (CF) from destination.
x86.instr.inc.description: Adds 1 to destination. Note: Carry Flag (CF) is preserved (not affected).
x86.instr.dec.description: Subtracts 1 from destination. Note: Carry Flag (CF) is preserved (not affected).
x86.instr.neg.description: Replaces operand with its two's complement (subtracts from 0). Sets CF=1 unless operand is 0.
x86.instr.cmp.description: Subtracts source from destination only to update flags (operands remain unchanged). Used before conditional jumps.
x86.instr.mul.description: Multiplies AL (byte), AX (word), or EAX by operand. 8-bit result in AX; 16-bit result in DX:AX; 32-bit in EDX:EAX.
x86.instr.imul.description: Performs signed multiplication. Supports 1, 2, or 3 operands in modern x86.
x86.instr.div.description: Divides AX by 8-bit operand (AL=quotient, AH=remainder) or DX:AX by 16-bit operand (AX=quotient, DX=remainder). Triggers INT 0 if division by zero.
x86.instr.idiv.description: Signed division of AX or DX:AX. Remember to use CBW or CWD before IDIV to sign-extend the dividend.
x86.instr.cbw.description: Sign-extends AL into AX (copies bit 7 of AL into all bits of AH).
x86.instr.cwd.description: Sign-extends AX into DX:AX (copies bit 15 of AX into all bits of DX). Essential before 16-bit IDIV.
x86.instr.cdq.description: Sign-extends EAX into EDX:EAX (64-bit pair). Essential before 32-bit IDIV. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.cqo.description: Sign-extends RAX into RDX:RAX (128 bits). Requires x86-64.
x86.instr.cdqe.description: Sign-extends 32-bit EAX to 64-bit RAX. Requires x86-64.
x86.instr.aaa.description: Adjusts the result of an ADD in AL to unpacked BCD format. Sets AH to carry if AL > 9.
x86.instr.aas.description: Adjusts the result of a SUB in AL to unpacked BCD format.
x86.instr.aam.description: Unpacks AL into AH:AL by dividing AL by 10 (or immediate base). AH=tens, AL=units.
x86.instr.aad.description: Packs unpacked BCD digits in AH:AL into AL by multiplying AH by 10 and adding to AL.
x86.instr.daa.description: Adjusts result of ADD in AL into valid Packed BCD digits.
x86.instr.das.description: Adjusts result of SUB in AL into valid Packed BCD digits.
x86.instr.and.description: Performs bitwise AND. Clears OF and CF; updates SF, ZF, and PF.
x86.instr.or.description: Performs bitwise OR. Clears OF and CF; updates SF, ZF, and PF.
x86.instr.xor.description: Performs bitwise XOR. Commonly used with same register (e.g. XOR AX, AX) to clear to 0 in fewer bytes.
x86.instr.not.description: Inverts all bits of the operand. Flags are NOT affected.
x86.instr.test.description: Performs bitwise AND to set flags (SF, ZF, PF) without modifying the operands.
x86.instr.shl.description: Shifts bits left, filling lowest bits with 0. Highest bit shifted out into CF.
x86.instr.shr.description: Shifts bits right, filling highest bits with 0. Lowest bit shifted out into CF.
x86.instr.sar.description: Shifts bits right preserving the sign bit (copies highest bit). Equivalent to signed integer division by 2.
x86.instr.rol.description: Rotates bits left circular fashion. Highest bit wraps around to bit 0 and CF.
x86.instr.ror.description: Rotates bits right circular fashion. Bit 0 wraps around to highest bit and CF.
x86.instr.rcl.description: Rotates bits left through CF (9-bit or 17-bit circular shift). CF becomes bit 0, old MSB becomes CF.
x86.instr.rcr.description: Rotates bits right through CF (9-bit or 17-bit circular shift). CF becomes MSB, bit 0 becomes CF.
x86.instr.shld.description: Shifts destination left, filling lower bits with the most significant bits of the source register.
x86.instr.shrd.description: Shifts destination right, filling upper bits with the least significant bits of the source register.
x86.instr.jmp.description: Transfers program execution unconditionally to target address.
x86.instr.call.description: Pushes return address onto stack and transfers control to the procedure.
x86.instr.ret.description: Pops return address from stack and transfers control back to caller.
x86.instr.retf.description: Pops both the offset and the segment of the return address, so it returns from a FAR procedure. Using it to leave a NEAR procedure unbalances the stack.
x86.instr.je.summary: Jump if Equal / Jump if Zero
x86.instr.je.description: Jumps to target label if ZF=1 (after CMP or arithmetic). Identical to JZ.
x86.instr.jz.description: Jumps to target label if Zero Flag is set (ZF=1). Identical to JE.
x86.instr.jne.summary: Jump if Not Equal / Jump if Not Zero
x86.instr.jne.description: Jumps to target label if ZF=0. Identical to JNZ.
x86.instr.jnz.description: Jumps to target label if Zero Flag is clear (ZF=0).
x86.instr.ja.description: Jumps if CF=0 and ZF=0 (unsigned greater than).
x86.instr.jae.description: Jumps if CF=0 (unsigned greater than or equal / not carry).
x86.instr.jb.description: Jumps if CF=1 (unsigned less than / carry).
x86.instr.jbe.description: Jumps if CF=1 or ZF=1 (unsigned less than or equal).
x86.instr.jc.description: Jumps if Carry Flag is set (CF=1). Useful after arithmetic or shift operations.
x86.instr.jnc.description: Jumps if Carry Flag is clear (CF=0).
x86.instr.jg.description: Jumps if ZF=0 and SF=OF (signed strictly greater than).
x86.instr.jge.description: Jumps if SF=OF (signed greater than or equal).
x86.instr.jl.description: Jumps if SF != OF (signed strictly less than).
x86.instr.jle.description: Jumps if ZF=1 or SF != OF (signed less than or equal).
x86.instr.js.description: Jumps if Sign Flag is set (SF=1, meaning result is negative in two's complement).
x86.instr.jns.description: Jumps if Sign Flag is clear (SF=0, meaning result is positive or zero).
x86.instr.jo.description: Jumps if Overflow Flag is set (OF=1, signed arithmetic overflow).
x86.instr.jno.description: Jumps if Overflow Flag is clear (OF=0).
x86.instr.jp.description: Jumps if Parity Flag is set (PF=1, even number of 1-bits in lowest byte).
x86.instr.jnp.summary: Jump if Not Parity / Parity Odd
x86.instr.jnp.description: Jumps if Parity Flag is clear (PF=0, odd number of 1-bits in lowest byte).
x86.instr.jcxz.description: Jumps if CX register is 0 without altering flags. Great for guarding 16-bit loops against 0 iterations.
x86.instr.jecxz.description: Jumps if 32-bit ECX register is 0 without altering flags. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.jrcxz.description: Jumps if 64-bit RCX register is 0 without altering flags. Requires x86-64.
x86.instr.loop.description: Decrements CX by 1 and jumps if CX != 0.
x86.instr.loope.summary: Loop while Equal / Loop while Zero
x86.instr.loope.description: Decrements CX by 1, and jumps if CX != 0 and ZF=1. Useful for string searching.
x86.instr.loopne.description: Decrements CX by 1, and jumps if CX != 0 and ZF=0.
x86.instr.sete.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the previous comparison found the two values equal (ZF=1), and 0 when it did not. Where a conditional jump chooses a path, SETcc turns the same condition into a value you can keep. Identical to SETZ.
x86.instr.setz.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Zero flag is set (ZF=1), and 0 otherwise. Identical to SETE, named after the flag rather than after the comparison.
x86.instr.setne.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the previous comparison found the two values different (ZF=0), and 0 when it did not. Identical to SETNZ.
x86.instr.setnz.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Zero flag is clear (ZF=0), and 0 otherwise. Identical to SETNE.
x86.instr.seta.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the previous unsigned comparison came out strictly greater (CF=0 and ZF=0), and 0 otherwise. SETG is the signed counterpart.
x86.instr.setae.summary: Set byte if Above or Equal (unsigned >=)
x86.instr.setae.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the unsigned comparison needed no borrow (CF=0), that is, greater or equal, and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.setb.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the unsigned comparison needed a borrow (CF=1), that is, strictly smaller, and 0 otherwise. SETL is the signed counterpart.
x86.instr.setbe.summary: Set byte if Below or Equal (unsigned <=)
x86.instr.setbe.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the unsigned comparison came out smaller or equal (CF=1 or ZF=1), and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.setc.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Carry flag is set (CF=1), and 0 otherwise. Handy for capturing the carry out of an addition as a number to add on. Identical to SETB.
x86.instr.setnc.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Carry flag is clear (CF=0), and 0 otherwise. Identical to SETAE.
x86.instr.setg.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the signed comparison came out strictly greater (ZF=0 and SF equal to OF), and 0 otherwise. Use it on signed numbers; SETA is the unsigned counterpart.
x86.instr.setge.summary: Set byte if Greater or Equal (signed >=)
x86.instr.setge.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the signed comparison came out greater or equal (SF equal to OF), and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.setl.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the signed comparison came out strictly smaller (SF different from OF), and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.setle.summary: Set byte if Less or Equal (signed <=)
x86.instr.setle.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the signed comparison came out smaller or equal (ZF=1, or SF different from OF), and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.sets.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Sign flag is set (SF=1), that is, the last result had its highest bit on, and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.setns.summary: Set byte if Not Sign / Non-negative
x86.instr.setns.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Sign flag is clear (SF=0), and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.seto.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Overflow flag is set (OF=1), that is, the last signed operation did not fit in its destination, and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.setno.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Overflow flag is clear (OF=0), and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.setp.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Parity flag is set (PF=1), that is, the low byte of the last result held an even number of one bits, and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.setnp.description: Writes 1 into the byte operand when the Parity flag is clear (PF=0), and 0 otherwise.
x86.instr.movsb.summary: Move byte from string to string
x86.instr.movsb.description: Copies byte from DS:[SI] to ES:[DI]. Increments/decrements SI and DI based on DF.
x86.instr.movsw.summary: Move word from string to string
x86.instr.movsw.description: Copies 16-bit word from DS:[SI] to ES:[DI] and updates SI and DI by 2 according to DF.
x86.instr.movsd.description: Copies 32-bit dword from DS:[ESI] to ES:[EDI] and advances pointers by 4. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.lodsb.summary: Load byte from string into AL
x86.instr.lodsb.description: Loads byte at DS:[SI] into AL and advances SI according to DF.
x86.instr.lodsw.summary: Load word from string into AX
x86.instr.lodsw.description: Loads 16-bit word at DS:[SI] into AX and advances SI by 2.
x86.instr.lodsd.description: Loads 32-bit dword at DS:[ESI] into EAX and advances ESI by 4. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.stosb.description: Stores byte in AL at ES:[DI] and advances DI according to DF.
x86.instr.stosw.description: Stores 16-bit word in AX at ES:[DI] and advances DI by 2.
x86.instr.stosd.description: Stores 32-bit dword in EAX at ES:[EDI] and advances EDI by 4. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.cmpsb.description: Compares DS:[SI] with ES:[DI] and updates flags.
x86.instr.cmpsw.description: Compares 16-bit word DS:[SI] with ES:[DI] and advances pointers by 2.
x86.instr.cmpsd.description: Compares 32-bit dwords DS:[ESI] with ES:[EDI] and advances pointers by 4. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.scasb.summary: Scan string for byte matching AL
x86.instr.scasb.description: Compares AL with ES:[DI] and advances DI.
x86.instr.scasw.summary: Scan string for word matching AX
x86.instr.scasw.description: Compares AX with word at ES:[DI] and advances DI by 2.
x86.instr.scasd.summary: Scan string for dword matching EAX
x86.instr.scasd.description: Compares EAX with dword at ES:[EDI] and advances EDI by 4. Requires 80386+.
x86.instr.movs.description: Generic form of MOVSB/MOVSW: copies from DS:[SI] to ES:[DI] and takes the element size from the declared operands instead of from the mnemonic.
x86.instr.cmps.description: Generic form of CMPSB/CMPSW: compares DS:[SI] with ES:[DI] and takes the element size from the declared operands.
x86.instr.lods.summary: Load string element into the accumulator
x86.instr.lods.description: Generic form of LODSB/LODSW: loads DS:[SI] into AL or AX according to the operand size and advances SI.
x86.instr.stos.summary: Store the accumulator into a string
x86.instr.stos.description: Generic form of STOSB/STOSW: stores AL or AX into ES:[DI] according to the operand size and advances DI.
x86.instr.scas.summary: Scan a string for the accumulator
x86.instr.scas.description: Generic form of SCASB/SCASW: compares AL or AX with ES:[DI] according to the operand size and advances DI.
x86.instr.rep.description: Prefix that repeats the string instruction that follows it and decrements CX on every pass. REP stops when CX reaches 0; REPE/REPZ also stop when ZF becomes 0, and REPNE/REPNZ when ZF becomes 1, so those two are the forms used with CMPS and SCAS.
x86.instr.cmc.description: Toggles the Carry Flag: sets CF to 0 if it was 1, or to 1 if it was 0.
x86.instr.cld.description: Sets Direction Flag to 0 so string operations auto-increment SI and DI.
x86.instr.std.description: Sets Direction Flag to 1 so string operations auto-decrement SI and DI.
x86.instr.cli.description: Disables maskable hardware interrupts. Essential in critical sections.
x86.instr.lahf.description: Copies SF, ZF, AF, PF, and CF from the FLAGS register into bits 7, 6, 4, 2, and 0 of AH.
x86.instr.sahf.description: Loads bits 7, 6, 4, 2, and 0 of AH into flags SF, ZF, AF, PF, and CF. Often used with coprocessor (FPU) comparisons.
x86.instr.nop.description: Performs no action. One-byte instruction (0x90) useful for timing, padding, or code patching.
x86.instr.hlt.description: Stops instruction execution until the next interrupt (hardware interrupt or reset) arrives.
x86.instr.wait.description: Causes the processor to wait until the numeric coprocessor (FPU) has finished current operation.
x86.instr.lock.description: Instruction prefix that locks the system bus, ensuring atomicity of read-modify-write memory operations in multiprocessor setups.
x86.instr.bsf.description: Scans source operand for first set bit (1) starting from bit 0 and stores index in destination.
x86.instr.bsr.description: Scans source operand for first set bit (1) starting from MSB and stores index in destination.
x86.instr.bt.description: Copies the specified bit of the first operand into the Carry Flag (CF).
x86.instr.btc.description: Saves the specified bit into CF and then inverts (complements) that bit in destination.
x86.instr.btr.description: Saves the specified bit into CF and then clears (resets) that bit in destination.
x86.instr.bts.description: Saves the specified bit into CF and then sets that bit to 1 in destination.
x86.instr.in.description: Reads a byte, word, or dword from an I/O port into AL, AX, or EAX.
x86.instr.out.description: Writes a byte, word, or dword from AL, AX, or EAX to an I/O port.
x86.instr.ins.description: Transfers a byte, word, or dword from the I/O port specified in DX into ES:[DI].
x86.instr.outs.description: Transfers a byte, word, or dword from DS:[SI] to the I/O port specified in DX.
x86.instr.int.description: Generates software interrupt. Clears IF and TF. INT 21h invokes DOS API services; INT 10h controls BIOS video.
x86.instr.into.description: Generates software interrupt 4 (INT 4) if the Overflow Flag (OF=1).
x86.instr.iret.description: Pops IP, CS, and the FLAGS register from stack to restore pre-interrupt state.
x86.instr.bound.description: Checks that a signed array index in reg16 is within limits [mem16, mem16+2]. Generates INT 5 if out of bounds.
x86.instr.arpl.description: Adjusts the Requested Privilege Level (RPL) of a selector to ensure it is not higher than caller.
x86.instr.lar.description: Loads the access rights byte from a segment descriptor into the destination register.
x86.instr.lsl.description: Loads the segment limit from a segment descriptor into the destination register.
x86.instr.cpuid.description: Returns processor details, family, model, stepping, and feature flags in EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX based on input in EAX.
x86.instr.rdtsc.description: Loads current 64-bit CPU cycle count into EDX:EAX. Indispensable for high-precision benchmarking and performance profiling.
x86.instr.ud2.description: Guaranteed to generate an invalid opcode exception (#UD). Compilers use it to trap unreachable code or assert failures.
x86.instr.syscall.description: Fast transition to 64-bit OS kernel (replaces INT 80h / INT 21h in 64-bit mode on x86-64 Linux and modern Windows).
x86.instr.sysret.description: Returns from 64-bit kernel mode to user space. Companion to SYSCALL.
x86.instr.fld.summary: Load floating-point value onto the stack
x86.instr.fld.description: Pushes a real number onto the x87 stack: the value becomes the new ST(0) and everything already there moves down one place. The operand may be another stack register or a 4, 8 or 10 byte real in memory.
x86.instr.fst.summary: Store top of stack without popping
x86.instr.fst.description: Copies ST(0) to the destination and leaves the stack as it was, so the value stays available for the next operation. Use FSTP instead when you are done with it.
x86.instr.fstp.summary: Store top of stack and pop
x86.instr.fstp.description: Copies ST(0) to the destination and then pops the stack, so ST(1) becomes the new top. Forgetting the pop is the usual cause of a stack that slowly fills up and overflows.
x86.instr.fadd.description: Adds the source to the destination stack register, or adds a real number in memory to ST(0). With no memory operand the result is left in the register named first.
x86.instr.fsub.description: Subtracts the source from the destination. The order matters and is easy to get backwards: FSUB leaves destination minus source, so with a memory operand it computes ST(0) minus that number.
x86.instr.fmul.description: Multiplies the destination by the source, or multiplies ST(0) by a real number in memory.
x86.instr.fdiv.description: Divides the destination by the source, leaving destination divided by source. Dividing by zero raises the x87 zero-divide exception instead of the CPU interrupt that DIV would raise.
x86.instr.fcom.description: Compares ST(0) with the operand and records the outcome in the condition bits C0, C2 and C3 of the status word. The CPU flags are untouched, so branching on the result takes FSTSW AX followed by SAHF.
x86.instr.fcomp.summary: Compare with top of stack and pop
x86.instr.fcomp.description: Does what FCOM does and then pops the stack, which is what you want when the compared value is no longer needed.
x86.instr.ftst.summary: Test top of stack against zero
x86.instr.ftst.description: Compares ST(0) against 0.0 and records the outcome in the condition bits, the floating-point counterpart of comparing an integer register against zero.
x86.instr.fild.summary: Load integer and convert to floating point
x86.instr.fild.description: Reads a 2, 4 or 8 byte signed integer from memory, converts it to the internal real format and pushes it. This is the usual bridge from the integer part of a program into the x87.
x86.instr.fist.description: Converts ST(0) to a signed integer and stores it, leaving the stack untouched. The conversion rounds according to the control word, which rounds to nearest unless you change it, so it does not simply drop the fraction.
x86.instr.fistp.description: Converts ST(0) to a signed integer, stores it and pops the stack: the usual last step when a floating-point result has to go back to the integer world.
x86.instr.fchs.summary: Change sign of top of stack
x86.instr.fchs.description: Flips the sign bit of ST(0), turning a positive value negative and a negative one positive. It is the floating-point counterpart of NEG.
x86.instr.fabs.summary: Absolute value of top of stack
x86.instr.fabs.description: Clears the sign bit of ST(0), so the value is left positive whatever it was.
x86.instr.fsqrt.summary: Square root of top of stack
x86.instr.fsqrt.description: Replaces ST(0) with its square root, in one instruction and to the full precision of the unit. A negative operand raises the invalid-operation exception. Availability note: The FSQRT instruction is unavailable in the integrated emu8086 emulator because its execution engine only simulates the 8086 CPU without the 8087 numeric coprocessor, triggering an invalid opcode trap. To execute programs using x87 instructions use DOSBox, real hardware, or native profiles.
x86.instr.fldz.description: Pushes 0.0 onto the stack. Using it costs less and reads better than keeping a zero in memory to load.
x86.instr.fld1.description: Pushes 1.0 onto the stack, the usual starting value for a running product or a factorial.
x86.instr.fldpi.description: Pushes pi onto the stack with the full internal precision of the unit, which is more exact than any constant you would reasonably type into the source.
x86.instr.fxch.description: Swaps ST(0) with another stack register, ST(1) when no operand is given. It is how you get an operand to the top when an instruction needs it there, most often to fix the order of a subtraction or a division.
x86.instr.finit.description: Resets the x87 to a known state: empty stack, default control word and cleared exceptions. It waits for any pending exception first. A program that uses the unit should run it once before the first floating-point instruction.
x86.instr.fninit.description: Does what FINIT does but without first waiting for a pending exception to be handled. The N in the name marks every no-wait form; prefer FINIT unless you are deliberately discarding a pending error.
x86.instr.fstsw.description: Copies the x87 status word, condition bits included, into AX or into memory. FSTSW AX followed by SAHF is the standard way to turn a floating-point comparison into CPU flags a conditional jump can read.
x86.instr.salc.description: Undocumented instruction (opcode 0xD6) present since the original 8086 processor. If CF = 0, sets AL = 00h; if CF = 1, sets AL = FFh. Flags are unaffected. Source: The Undocumented PC (Frank van Gilluwe).
x86.instr.icebp.description: Undocumented instruction (opcode 0xF1), also known as INT1. Triggers a single-byte debug trap (vector 1) originally designed for In-Circuit Emulator (ICE) hardware debuggers. Source: Intel SDM Vol 2 / The Undocumented PC.
x86.instr.lgdt.description: Loads the base address and limit of the Global Descriptor Table (GDT) into the GDTR register. Privileged system instruction (Ring 0).
x86.instr.lidt.description: Loads the base address and limit of the Interrupt Descriptor Table (IDT) into the IDTR register. Privileged system instruction (Ring 0).
x86.instr.lmsw.description: Loads the lower 4 bits of the Machine Status Word (CR0 bits 0-3). Historically used on the 80286 to switch into protected mode (PE bit). Privileged.
x86.instr.smsw.description: Stores the lower 16 bits of the machine status word (CR0 register) into a general-purpose register or memory.
x86.instr.sldt.description: Stores the segment selector from the LDTR register into a register or memory location.
x86.instr.str.description: Stores the segment selector from the task register TR into a 16-bit register or memory.
x86.instr.verr.description: Verifies whether the segment indicated by a selector is readable at the current privilege level. Sets ZF=1 if valid.
x86.instr.verw.description: Verifies whether the segment indicated by a selector is writable at the current privilege level. Sets ZF=1 if valid.
x86.instr.clts.description: Clears the TS (Task Switched) bit in CR0. Used by exception handlers during coprocessor context switches.
x86.instr.invlpg.description: Invalidates the translation lookaside buffer (TLB) cache entry corresponding to the specified virtual address.
x86.instr.rdmsr.description: Reads the 64-bit Model Specific Register (MSR) indexed by ECX into the EDX:EAX register pair. Ring 0.
x86.instr.wrmsr.description: Writes the 64-bit value in EDX:EAX to the Model Specific Register (MSR) specified in ECX. Ring 0.
x86.instr.rsm.description: Restores the processor state saved when entering System Management Mode (SMM) and resumes standard execution.
x86.instr.sysenter.description: Executes a fast, low-overhead transition from user mode (Ring 3) to kernel mode (Ring 0) using pre-programmed MSRs.
x86.instr.sysexit.description: Executes a fast return from kernel mode (Ring 0) to user mode (Ring 3).
x86.instr.swapgs.description: Exchanges the current GS base register value with the value stored in the IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE MSR. Ring 0.
x86.instr.rdtscp.summary: Read Time-Stamp Counter and Processor ID
x86.instr.rdtscp.description: Reads the performance counter into EDX:EAX and the processor core ID into ECX as an atomic, serializing instruction.
x86.instr.emms.description: Marks all x87 FPU stack registers as empty. Mandatory before executing floating-point instructions after using MMX.
x86.instr.movd.description: Transfers 32 integer bits between a general-purpose register/memory and the low part of an MMX or XMM register.
x86.instr.movq.description: Transfers 64 integer bits between memory or MMX/XMM registers.
x86.instr.paddb.description: Performs parallel independent addition of 8 packed unsigned bytes with wraparound overflow.
x86.instr.paddw.description: Performs parallel independent addition of 4 packed 16-bit words.
x86.instr.paddd.description: Performs parallel independent addition of 2 packed 32-bit doublewords.
x86.instr.pxor.summary: Bitwise Logical XOR of Packed SIMD Values
x86.instr.pxor.description: Computes bitwise logical XOR between MMX or XMM registers. Frequently used as pxor xmm0, xmm0 to zero a register.
x86.instr.pcmpeqb.description: Compares packed bytes; writes FFh for equal bytes and 00h for unequal bytes.
x86.instr.movss.description: Copies a 32-bit IEEE 754 single-precision float between memory and the low bits of an XMM register.
x86.instr.addss.description: Adds the scalar 32-bit floating-point numbers in the low 32 bits of two XMM registers.
x86.instr.addsd.description: Adds the scalar 64-bit floating-point values in the low 64 bits of two XMM registers. Foundation of modern 64-bit math.
x86.instr.mulsd.description: Multiplies two 64-bit scalar double-precision floats in the low bits of XMM registers.
x86.instr.comisd.summary: Compare Scalar Double-Precision and Set CPU Flags
x86.instr.comisd.description: Compares two 64-bit floating-point values and sets the CPU EFLAGS (ZF, PF, CF) directly, allowing immediate conditional jumps.
x86.instr.ucomisd.description: Compares two 64-bit scalar floats without raising an invalid operation exception on quiet NaNs.
x86.instr.cvtsi2sd.description: Converts a signed 32-bit or 64-bit integer into a 64-bit double-precision floating-point value in an XMM register.
x86.instr.cvtsd2si.description: Converts a 64-bit double-precision floating-point value into a signed integer in a general-purpose register.
x86.instr.movaps.description: Transfers four 32-bit floats between XMM registers or 16-byte aligned memory. Triggers a #GP fault if memory is unaligned.
x86.instr.movups.description: Transfers four 32-bit floats between XMM registers and memory without requiring 16-byte alignment.
x86.instr.movdqa.summary: Move Aligned Packed Integer Double Quadword (128-bit)
x86.instr.movdqa.description: Transfers 128 packed bits between XMM registers and 16-byte aligned memory.
x86.instr.movdqu.summary: Move Unaligned Packed Integer Double Quadword (128-bit)
x86.instr.movdqu.description: Transfers 128 packed bits between XMM registers and unaligned memory.
x86.instr.addps.description: Performs parallel addition of four 32-bit floating-point numbers across 128-bit XMM registers.
x86.instr.mulps.description: Performs parallel multiplication of four 32-bit floats in XMM registers.
x86.instr.divps.description: Performs parallel division of four 32-bit floats in XMM registers.
x86.instr.sqrtps.summary: Square Root of Packed Single-Precision Floats (4x32-bit)
x86.instr.sqrtps.description: Calculates the parallel square root of four 32-bit floats in an XMM register.
x86.instr.xorps.summary: Bitwise Logical XOR of Packed Single-Precision Floats
x86.instr.xorps.description: Performs bitwise logical XOR across 128-bit XMM registers. Frequently used to toggle floating-point signs.
x86.instr.andps.summary: Bitwise Logical AND of Packed Single-Precision Floats
x86.instr.andps.description: Performs bitwise logical AND across 128-bit XMM registers.
x86.instr.ldmxcsr.summary: Load MXCSR Control and Status Register
x86.instr.ldmxcsr.description: Loads rounding modes and exception masks into the SIMD control/status register MXCSR from memory.
x86.instr.stmxcsr.summary: Store MXCSR Control and Status Register
x86.instr.stmxcsr.description: Stores the contents of the SIMD control/status register MXCSR into memory.
x86.instr.fxsave.summary: Save x87 and SIMD State (512 bytes)
x86.instr.fxsave.description: Saves the complete state of x87 FPU, MMX, and XMM registers into a 512-byte memory layout.
x86.instr.fxrstor.summary: Restore x87 and SIMD State (512 bytes)
x86.instr.fxrstor.description: Restores the complete state of x87 FPU and SIMD registers from a 512-byte memory layout.
x86.instr.pshufb.description: Shuffles or clears each byte in an XMM register according to an index byte mask.
x86.instr.vaddps.summary: AVX Vector Add Packed Single-Precision Floats (VEX)
x86.instr.vaddps.description: 3-operand AVX vector addition with VEX prefix encoding (CPUID.01H:ECX.AVX[bit 28]). Not covered in depth in this version as it is outside the introductory curriculum.
x86.instr.vmovaps.summary: AVX Move Aligned Packed Single Floats (256-bit)
x86.instr.vmovaps.description: AVX vector move for eight 32-bit floats with VEX encoding. Not covered in depth in this version as it is outside the introductory curriculum.
x86.instr.vzeroupper.summary: Zero Upper 128 Bits of YMM Registers (AVX)
x86.instr.vzeroupper.description: Zeros the upper 128 bits of all YMM registers to prevent execution penalties when transitioning between AVX and legacy SSE code.
x86.instr.vpxor.description: 3-operand AVX vector bitwise XOR across 256-bit YMM registers. Not covered in depth in this version as it is outside the introductory curriculum.
x86.instr.lldt.description: Loads the segment selector for the LDT into the LDTR register. Privileged instruction executed at Ring 0.
x86.instr.ltr.description: Loads the segment selector for the Task State Segment (TSS) into the task register TR. Privileged Ring 0 instruction.
x86.instr.sgdt.description: Stores the limit and base address of the GDTR register into memory.
x86.instr.sidt.description: Stores the limit and base address of the IDTR register into memory.
x86.instr.invd.description: Invalidates all internal processor cache lines without flushing modified dirty data back to main memory. Privileged.
x86.instr.wbinvd.description: Writes back all modified cache lines to main memory and invalidates internal caches. Privileged instruction.
x86.instr.subps.description: Subtracts four packed single-precision floating-point numbers (32-bit each) from source into destination using 128-bit XMM registers.
x86.instr.maxps.summary: Maximum of Packed Single-Precision Floating-Point Values
x86.instr.maxps.description: Computes the component-wise maximum between four 32-bit floating-point numbers in 128-bit XMM registers.
x86.instr.minps.summary: Minimum of Packed Single-Precision Floating-Point Values
x86.instr.minps.description: Computes the component-wise minimum between four 32-bit floating-point numbers in 128-bit XMM registers.
x86.instr.rcpps.summary: Compute Reciprocals of Packed Single-Precision Floating-Point Values
x86.instr.rcpps.description: Computes an approximate reciprocal (1/x) for each of the four single-precision floating-point values in a 128-bit XMM register.
x86.instr.rsqrtps.summary: Compute Reciprocals of Square Roots of Packed Single-Precision Values
x86.instr.rsqrtps.description: Computes an approximate 1/sqrt(x) for each of four single-precision floats in a 128-bit XMM register.
x86.instr.movapd.summary: Move Aligned Packed Double-Precision Floating-Point Values
x86.instr.movapd.description: Transfers 128 bits (two 64-bit double-precision floats) between XMM registers or 16-byte aligned memory.
x86.instr.movupd.summary: Move Unaligned Packed Double-Precision Floating-Point Values
x86.instr.movupd.description: Transfers 128 bits (two double-precision floats) between XMM registers or unaligned memory.
x86.instr.addpd.description: Adds two packed double-precision floating-point numbers (64-bit each) in 128-bit XMM registers (SSE2).
x86.instr.subpd.description: Subtracts two packed double-precision floating-point numbers (64-bit each) in 128-bit XMM registers (SSE2).
x86.instr.mulpd.description: Multiplies two packed double-precision floating-point numbers (64-bit each) in 128-bit XMM registers (SSE2).
x86.instr.divpd.description: Divides two packed double-precision floating-point numbers (64-bit each) in 128-bit XMM registers (SSE2).
x86.instr.paddq.description: Adds packed 64-bit integers (quadwords) in 128-bit XMM registers (SSE2).
x86.instr.psubq.description: Subtracts packed 64-bit integers (quadwords) in 128-bit XMM registers (SSE2).
x86.instr.addsubps.description: Subtracts odd components and adds even components between 128-bit XMM registers. Ideal for complex number arithmetic.
x86.instr.haddps.description: Horizontally adds adjacent pairs of 32-bit floats across two source operands into a 128-bit XMM register.
x86.instr.dpps.summary: Dot Product of Packed Single-Precision Floats (SSE4.1)
x86.instr.dpps.description: Calculates the conditional dot product of 4-element single-precision float vectors based on an immediate mask.
x86.instr.roundps.description: Rounds four packed 32-bit floats in an XMM register according to the rounding mode specified in the immediate byte.
x86.instr.pcmpestri.summary: Packed Compare Explicit-Length Strings, Return Index (SSE4.2)
x86.instr.pcmpestri.description: Performs packed comparison on explicit-length strings specified in EAX/EDX, returning an index in ECX and setting status flags.
x86.instr.crc32.description: Accumulates a cyclic redundancy check (CRC) 32-bit value using the iSCSI polynomial over a source operand.
x86.instr.vmulps.summary: AVX Multiply Packed Single-Precision Floats (3 operands)
x86.instr.vmulps.description: Multiplies up to eight 32-bit floats across 256-bit YMM registers using VEX encoding and 3-operand non-destructive syntax.
x86.instr.vmovups.summary: AVX Move Unaligned Packed Single-Precision Floats
x86.instr.vmovups.description: Transfers 256-bit unaligned floating-point vectors between memory and YMM registers using VEX prefix.
x86.instr.vpaddd.summary: AVX2 Vector Add Packed Dword Integers in YMM
x86.instr.vpaddd.description: Adds eight signed 32-bit dwords across 256-bit YMM registers using AVX2 extension and VEX prefix.
